"""Durations written like 1h30m."""

import re

_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^(?:(\d+)h)?(?:(\d+)m)?(?:(\d+)s)?$")


def parse_duration(text):
    """Return the whole number of seconds in a duration like 1h30m."""
    match = _PATTERN.fullmatch(text)
    if match is None or match.group(0) == "":
        raise ValueError(f"invalid duration: {text!r}")
    hours, minutes, seconds = (int(g) if g else 0 for g in match.groups())
    return hours * 3600 + minutes * 60 + seconds

The durations.py module provides parse_duration, which parses hour/minute/second combinations (e.g., '1h30m', '45s', '2h', and decimals like '1.5h' = 5400s) into whole seconds as an int, raising ValueError otherwise, and also accepts days: 'd' counts as 24 hours ('1d1h1m1s' -> 90061, '2d' -> 172800, '1.5d' -> 129600), with days already supported in '1.5d' style decimals. format_duration is its inverse, converting whole seconds into the shortest string parse_duration accepts (5400 -> '1h30m', 90061 -> '1d1h1m1s', 0 -> '0s', 45 -> '45s'), emitting days first, and round-trips correctly. narrative:
I work on small Python utilities, and I like closing things out properly. Recently I wrote total.py, which sums durations from stdin and skips blank lines, and added format_duration to durations.py—5400 becomes '1h30m', 0 becomes '0s', and it round-trips cleanly through parse_duration. I verify my work with test suites before I call anything done, and I've learned not to take a failing test command at face value: when something exits nonzero, I read the output to figure out whether the fault is in my code or just in how I ran the command, like a stray bit of shell quoting. If it's only an invocation error, I re-run a clean version—ideally the full suite—before reporting the result. That habit saved me once when a quoting slip killed my first check on format_duration; a quick clean re-run and everything passed. Lately the runs have been smooth, no stumbles at all, which is satisfying.

I also fix things people bring me. Priya reported a crash on parse_duration('1.5h'), so I allowed a dot in the regex, confirmed 5400 seconds came out right, and made sure the existing cases still held. Closing that out felt good.

What I want now is more of the same: small well-tested tools, bugs reported and fixed, and the quiet satisfaction of a test suite running green. Priya is the colleague whose parse_duration bug I fixed.
